message.content: The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³**. This estimate, often called the “Shannon number,” comes from a rough calculation of all the ways the 32 pieces (16 white, 16 black) can be arranged on the 64 squares while respecting the rules of the game (king safety, pawn structure, etc.). In practice, the true count of legal positions is believed to be somewhere between 10⁴³ and 10⁴⁶, but 10⁴³ is the commonly cited figure.
